synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot reported a lost link after liftoff causing the UAS to crash into a tree.
narrative: After I performed a preflight inspection. I turned on the UAS and the controller. I waited for a few minutes while I obtained a GPS lock. Once the lock was obtained I launched the UAS from the ground at 10 ft I speed and prepared to do a controller test but the UAS started moving forward at a rapid pace. I had 0 control and watched the UAS crash into a tree. I was able to recover most of the parts. There was no injury or damage other then the UAS.

screening_note: The reporter explicitly describes lost link and successful return to home; the cause is the reporter's account.
synopsis: Government UAS pilot reported a cell phone booster tower caused interference with the UAS transmitter. A lost link occurred and the UAS successfully completed a RTH.
narrative: UAS; performing search and rescue training at 200 feet; went into a lost link and returned home within 10 seconds of the glitching screen. UAS RTH at programmed altitude without issue. Two UAS were flying in the general area (approx 500 feet apart); but the flight decks were within 25 feet of each other. A large monitor was being used by one member outside a command vehicle to take advantage of power and shade. Lost link and RTH occurred twice on back-to-back hops. After securing flights; the crew noticed a cellular antenna booster within 6 feet of the pilot in command; used by the command vehicle data terminal (non-uas). Repeated testing shows interference with the flight controller within 5 feet of the antenna.

synopsis: Government UAS pilot reported a lost link event during takeoff resulted in an airspace incursion before the pilot regained control and landed the UAS.
narrative: I was operating a DJI M30T and had just taken off at a beach location when at around 25' AGL the drone decided to take off vertically and I lost all control of the drone. The sticks were unresponsive. I force closed DroneSense; which was the app we fly in and entered the DJI Pilot app. While in this app; I was still unable to control the drone. I attempted to place the drone into RTH without success; the RTH initiated but did not respond. I also attempted to place the drone in Attitude Mode (ATTI); which also did not work. I then proceeded to toggle on and off the bottom Vision Positioning System (VPS) sensor; which was already off. After this; I attempted to regain control again and attempted to initiate another Return to Home. This time the drone responded; and I took over and landed the drone without further incident. The drone reached a max Alt of 1276 ft/389 meters AGL. The drone was only about 50 ft Horizontally away from me. We were in the process of calling ZZZ Tower when control was regained and the drone was landed. Camera feed was never lost during the incident. DroneSense replay shows stick inputs in an attempt to take control without any luck.
